content.value_statement: Azure Storage choices can be hard to compare across blobs, files, queues, tables, and data lake workloads. This skill gives practical service, tier, SDK, CLI, and authentication guidance.
actual_capabilities: Compares Blob Storage, File Shares, Queue Storage, Table Storage, and Data Lake use cases.
Explains Hot, Cool, Cold, Archive, Standard, and Premium storage tier tradeoffs.
Provides Azure MCP and Azure CLI references for storage accounts, containers, blobs, uploads, and downloads.
Summarizes SDK package names and quick-start patterns for Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, Rust, and .NET.
Gives authentication guidance for local development, managed identities, RBAC, and production credential selection.
limitations: Does not replace the Azure portal, Azure MCP server, or Azure CLI authentication flow.
Does not cover SQL databases, Cosmos DB design, Event Hubs, or Service Bus messaging.
Does not validate live Azure resource state unless connected tools are available and authorized.
Does not provide full SDK coverage for every advanced feature in every language.

use_cases.title: Choose a Storage Service
use_cases.description: Compare storage options for object data, file shares, queues, tables, and analytics workloads before implementation.

use_cases.title: Operate Blob Workflows
use_cases.description: Use MCP or CLI references to list accounts, inspect containers, and plan blob upload or download tasks.

use_cases.title: Build Storage Clients
use_cases.description: Find package names, authentication patterns, and SDK quick starts for common Azure Storage integrations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Azure Blob Storage, Azure Files, Queue Storage, Table Storage, and Data Lake for my workload. Ask me for missing requirements first.

prompt_templates.title: Select Access Tier
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend an Azure Blob access tier for data accessed about [frequency] and retained for [duration]. Include tradeoffs and lifecycle guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me list storage accounts, containers, and blobs using the preferred Azure MCP approach. Use CLI fallback only if MCP is unavailable.

prompt_templates.title: Design SDK Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Azure Storage SDK authentication approach for [language] in local development and production. Include managed identity and RBAC guidance.

output_examples.input: I need low-cost storage for backups that are rarely restored after six months.
output: Recommends Cold or Archive depending on restore expectations and latency tolerance.
Explains minimum retention and rehydration concerns before choosing Archive.
Suggests lifecycle management from Hot or Cool into colder tiers.

output_examples.input: I want to upload and download blobs from an authorized Azure account.
output: Prefers Azure MCP storage tools when enabled.
Identifies the needed account, container, blob name, and local path inputs.
Notes that CLI fallback requires authenticated Azure access and careful path selection.

output_examples.input: I am building a Python service that writes files to Azure Storage.
output: Points to the relevant Azure Storage SDK family and identity package.
Recommends DefaultAzureCredential only for local development.
Recommends managed identity and least-privilege RBAC for production.

best_practices: Use managed identity and least-privilege RBAC for production Azure-hosted workloads.
Choose storage tiers based on access frequency, retention period, restore latency, and lifecycle policy needs.
Prefer Azure MCP tools for live operations, and confirm account, container, blob, and path values before changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use DefaultAzureCredential as the production credential for Azure-hosted services.
Do not hardcode account keys, connection strings, SAS tokens, or customer data in prompts or files.
Do not use Azure Queue Storage when sessions, topics, ordering guarantees, or advanced broker features are required.

faq.question: What Azure services does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Blob Storage, Azure Files, Queue Storage, Table Storage, and Data Lake Storage Gen2.

faq.question: Can it manage my live Azure resources?
faq.answer: It can guide authorized MCP or CLI operations, but it does not bypass Azure authentication or permissions.

faq.question: Does it help choose Blob access tiers?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Hot, Cool, Cold, and Archive tiers based on access frequency, cost, and restore needs.

faq.question: Does it include SDK guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes package and quick-start references for several Azure Storage SDK languages.

faq.question: Should I use DefaultAzureCredential in production?
faq.answer: No. Use managed identity or another deterministic production credential with least-privilege RBAC.

faq.question: What is outside the scope of this skill?
faq.answer: It does not cover SQL databases, Cosmos DB design, Event Hubs, Service Bus, or full advanced SDK documentation.
